vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: In affected 2.1.X and 2.2.X, AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() reads an attacker-controlled class name and calls Class.forName(className, true, classLoader) before any acceptMatchers decision, permitting class initialization before rejection. The 2.1.12 and 2.2.7 patches move the matcher decision before that call.

atomic_bic.evidence: 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea added the late acceptMatchers check on 2.2.X, but did not first write the vulnerable deserialization/Class.forName behavior. Its parent already contains that behavior, and affected tags 2.1.0 through 2.1.9 and 2.2.0 through 2.2.3 predate the proposed BIC. Local blame traces the surviving readObject/Class.forName code through earlier moves and formatting commits to 2006-2007 history, which the primary did not close to a parent-absent atomic writer.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: 23e6ee17bae46bb8e7a76dd7aeb508ec89e76a25, the immediate parent of 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea, already calls Class.forName(className, true, classLoader) and then returns the resolved class without an allowlist. The primary itself records introducer_parent_absent=false, so its claimed BIC fails the required parent-absence gate.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea and the parallel 2.1.X late-check commit cdb59eb6131696a440870ab89ad0e20804eb5ca7 are single-parent public commits rather than merge objects; no squash decomposition is needed for those mitigation commits. This does not cure the atomic-BIC failure.

affected_release_membership.evidence: The vulnerable pre-filter Class.forName call is present in tags 2.1.0, 2.1.9, 2.1.10, 2.1.11, 2.2.0, 2.2.3, 2.2.4, and 2.2.6. 691a9df5 is first contained in 2.2.4, while cdb59eb6 is first contained in 2.1.10, proving that neither can explain the full advisory ranges beginning at 2.1.0 and 2.2.0.

fixed_release_membership.evidence: ba8c355d82a010d677455df43b49725d21dbd07a is an ancestor of 2.1.12 and not of 2.1.11; cca24d646c898adf7e01a765ebf6d677cc02b696 is an ancestor of 2.2.7 and not of 2.2.6. The fixed tags contain the pre-Class.forName matcher check.

direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched_state.evidence: The direct branch fixes are ba8c355d82a010d677455df43b49725d21dbd07a for 2.1.X and cca24d646c898adf7e01a765ebf6d677cc02b696 for 2.2.X. Their parents retain the late check, and each patch inserts acceptMatchers validation before class initialization.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The primary checks AI markers only on 691a9df5a0aff0dddeedc5181f6e5832ee90dcea, which is not a valid BIC. Human author/committer metadata and absent trailers on that incomplete mitigation cannot establish NOT_AI for the earlier, still-unresolved causal writer.

findings: The claimed introducer fails the protocol's immediate-parent absence test: its parent is already vulnerable.
The advisory's affected ranges include releases that predate both late-allowlist commits, so those commits cannot be the full-range atomic BICs.
The two direct fixes and their release membership are supported, but fix evidence does not substitute for BIC closure or BIC-only AI attribution.
remaining_gap: Trace the vulnerable getObject/ObjectInputStream/Class.forName lifecycle through the 2006-2007 ByteBuffer-to-IoBuffer-to-AbstractIoBuffer moves to the smallest public first writer, prove absence in its immediate parent, then inspect AI markers on that actual BIC. Until those gates close, fail closed rather than retaining NOT_AI.
